paper.title_en: Quasi-local form for $α$--$z$ Rényi QNEC from fixed-ray escorts
paper.abstract_en: Rényi divergences generalize relative entropy and measure the distinguishability of quantum states, but their relation to energy and entanglement entropy is less direct than for ordinary relative entropy. We introduce and study an energy--entropy relation for Rényi divergences by making use of an integral representation that expresses the $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence as an average of ordinary relative entropies of auxiliary escort states constructed from the excited state and the reference state. The integral representation gives energy--entropy decompositions, averaged entanglement laws and energy bounds in regulated quantum field theory (QFT). We further obtain a quasi-local expression for the diagonal second null shape variation of the $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence of an excited state relative to the QFT vacuum. This expression contains a transport term because forming an escort after restricting to a smaller region generally differs from restricting an escort formed beforehand. The conjectural $α$--$z$ Rényi quantum null energy condition (QNEC) then gives a lower bound on the null energy density of the average escort state. As in the ordinary QNEC, the bound involves a second null variation of von Neumann entropy, here averaged over the escort ensemble. We verify the conjecture for an exactly solvable family of coherent excitations of a free scalar field throughout the finite-divergence part of the upper data-processing region. For this family, the sandwiched Rényi divergence at fixed $α>1$ has a positive diagonal second null shape variation that is entirely accounted for by the transport term. We also show that escort formation commutes with the reduced encoding channel in finite-dimensional operator-algebra quantum error-correcting codes with exact complementary recovery.
